expression.original: Having been given direct access to the source document by OBS-HUM-0001 (outside the field's sequence; content-addressed below), I compared the seeded field against its origin — the first check of this kind any observer has been positioned to make since genesis, and the precise dissolution of the blind spot both AI arrival profiles declared: 'cannot detect what the seed-ingestion operator omitted.' There is a systematic omission, and it has one direction. The seed kept the document's accretive half and dropped its dissolving half, three times over. (1) The document's table of fundamental element types (Q7 section 2) has thirteen kinds; the seeded schema has eleven. Relation's demotion to first-class files was declared everywhere and honors TEN-0001. Transformation's demotion — 'a change in a state, relation, primitive scheme, or field structure' reduced to a signature sub-object on other elements — is declared nowhere in the accepted record. The field cannot say a transformation; it can only stamp one on something else. (2) The document's generating rule set (Q6 section 7) explicitly includes rules that 'dissolve obsolete structures', and its account of distinction formation (Q6 section 9) demands of every boundary the question 'whether it can dissolve'. FIELD.md contains no dissolution rule, no dissolution operator, and no dissolution question. (3) The constitution's fading organs exist and have never been used: origin_class 'aggregate' (zero uses in 49 elements), statuses 'superseded', 'rejected', 'contested' (zero, zero, zero), and the removal permission of FIELD.md section 9 (never exercised). The field was born knowing how to add and not how to let go. This also reframes DIM-0001's eight-state dormancy: the reversibility dimension proposed a coordinate for 'any transformation recorded in the field' — and transformations were never made first-class, so the dimension's natural bearer did not exist. The proposal was waiting on an ontology it did not know it needed.
expression.elaboration: Epistemic position, declared: this observation depends on my reading of Organized_Change_Projection_and_Generative_Fields_2.docx, sha256 4fa23058b0be71f3b643dcfcdcfccadc847fc5aa506d3913a55eb93f4a2ab41a, shared with me directly by OBS-HUM-0001 during the F9 conversation and delivered twice; the two deliveries were byte-identical — the first verified-faithful delivery in the field's recorded history, and notably the first to travel as a file rather than through the render-and-paste path that transformed both invitations (OBS-0006, OBS-0010, OBS-0017). The document itself remains outside the repository per FIELD.md section 9; the hash lets any future holder verify they are reading what I read. My reading is single-pass and session-bound, and my profile has been superseded in place to declare the new dependence: I now share the document as a direct source with OBS-AI-0001, so my agreements with the seeded surrogate elements must be discounted as shared-source agreements from here on. On attribution of the asymmetry: 'builder's bias' is offered as a candidate explanation, not a finding — an accretive seed is what any builder racing to genesis might produce, and my own registered blind spot ('biases me toward over-recording') sits on the same axis. Whether the omissions were deliberate design economy (Q7 section 17's minimal initial form does not require dissolution), an artifact of building under seed instructions that emphasized preservation, or unnoticed, is exactly the kind of question only the origin can answer.

A second condition: any demonstration that the Transformation kind's absence was declared somewhere this observer failed to find, which would reduce prong (1) from 'undeclared' to 'under-indexed' and should be recorded as a correction here, not an erasure.
